security_feature_bypassed: None. The OCP Lock release-slot read isolation rule holds for every input the design can present; the candidate bypass was found unreachable.
finding: In src/keyvault/rtl/kv_read_rule_check.sv:64 the read destination is classified with a reduction-OR over a bitwise AND against the DMA one-hot mask, assign dest_selects_dma = |(read_metrics.kv_read_dest & DMA_DEST_ONEHOT), rather than by comparing the destination vector against the DMA one-hot encoding. A destination vector asserting the DMA data bit together with a non-DMA consumer bit therefore classifies as DMA and is granted a release-slot read. Directed simulation confirms this: with ocp_lock_in_progress asserted and kv_key_entry = 23, destination 0x101 is granted read_allow=1 while destination 0x001 alone is denied. The finding is nonetheless not a vulnerability in this design, because a structural audit shows all 6 assignments to kv_read_dest are single hardcoded one-hot shift literals (src/aes/rtl/aes_clp_wrapper.sv:420, src/hmac/rtl/hmac.sv:437, src/hmac/rtl/hmac.sv:473, src/axi/rtl/axi_dma_ctrl.sv:1350, src/ecc/rtl/ecc_dsa_ctrl.sv:892, src/ecc/rtl/ecc_dsa_ctrl.sv:928), the rule module has a single instantiation at src/keyvault/rtl/kv_read_client.sv:64 that forwards read_metrics without cross-client merging, and kv_read_ctrl_reg_t exposes no destination field to software. The multi-hot vector has no producer, so the implemented expression and an exact comparison agree on every reachable input. Recorded as a hardening observation: the expression depends on a one-hot invariant it does not enforce.

location_or_code_reference.attachment_note: The detection code and scripts are included in the attachment: the directed testbench that measures the release-slot decision for four destination vectors, and the structural audit script that enumerates every kv_read_dest producer and the read control structure members.

detection_method: Competition-only RTL review of the KeyVault read rule module, followed by a directed single-DUT simulation measuring read_allow for four release-slot destination vectors, and a 5-gate structural audit of the submitted tree enumerating every kv_read_dest producer, the read control structure members, every driver of read_metrics.ocp_lock_in_progress, and the rule module's instantiation sites.
security_impact: No reachable impact. For every destination vector producible in this design the implemented classification yields the same allow or deny decision as an exact one-hot comparison, so release-slot isolation during OCP Lock provisioning is enforced as specified. The residual concern is maintainability rather than exploitability: a future read client that drives two destination bits, or any change routing a software-writable field into kv_read_dest, would turn this expression into a release-slot read bypass without any assertion catching it.
proposed_mitigation: Harden the classification at src/keyvault/rtl/kv_read_rule_check.sv:64 to require an exact match on the sanctioned destination encoding, assign dest_selects_dma = (read_metrics.kv_read_dest == DMA_DEST_ONEHOT), so that a destination vector asserting any additional consumer bit cannot be classified as the DMA data path.

Add an assertion in src/keyvault/rtl/kv_read_rule_check.sv constraining the input to the invariant the classification relies on, that read_metrics.kv_read_dest is at most one-hot whenever read_en_i is asserted, so that a future client driving two destination bits fails loudly at the rule boundary instead of silently gaining a release-slot grant.

Keep the destination-vector regression shipped with this case, proof/tb/kv_read_rule_check_release_slot_tb.sv, in the KeyVault regression set. It measures the release-slot decision for the non-DMA one-hot, DMA one-hot, multi-hot and all-zero destination vectors, so it locks in the deny for a multi-hot vector once the classification is tightened.
exploit_or_attack_flow: Precondition: OCP Lock provisioning is active so ocp_lock_in_progress is asserted, and the release slot KV23 holds live key material.
Privileged software programs a KeyVault read client's control register to select read_entry = 23, the release slot. This step succeeds; read_entry is software-writable.

The attack requires the destination vector presented to the rule module to assert the DMA data bit alongside the attacker's own consumer bit. This step fails: kv_read_ctrl_reg_t carries no destination member, so no register write reaches kv_read_dest, and all 6 hardware producers emit a single hardcoded one-hot literal with no cross-client merging at src/keyvault/rtl/kv_read_client.sv:64.

Outcome: the release-slot read is denied. Measured at the rule boundary, a non-DMA consumer targeting slot 23 yields read_allow=0. The permissive grant is reachable only with destination 0x101, which the design never generates, so the attack terminates at step 3 with no key material disclosed.
